subject: maths-aa-sl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Radians, arcs and sectors
bigPicture: Radians measure angles by arc length on a unit circle. They make arc and sector formulas simple and are required for calculus with trig.

keyTerms.def: angle subtending an arc equal to the radius

workedExamples.title: Segment area
workedExamples.prompt: r = 6, θ = π/3. Find the segment area.

practice.prompt: A sector has radius 5 cm and perimeter 16 cm. Find θ and the area.
A pendulum 0.8 m long swings through 35°. Find the arc length.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

given.item: Arc length and sector area in radians

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.

linkingQuestions.prompt: Why do exact values use multiples of π/6 and π/4?
